Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

less adverb and adjective

also fewer, less than, more or less, less than (a number), a little under, fewer than

classical

Ov. Rem. 94: crās minus aptus erit
Liv. praef. 12: quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat
Cic. Div. 1.68: minus XXX diēbus (Lewis & Short)

minus

adverb; as a noun with a genitive, “less of”: minus pecūniae

Before a number it often stands without quam, and the number keeps the case the sentence needs: minus XXX diēbus, in less than thirty days; paulō minus septingentī, a little under seven hundred, as subject. “The less …, the less …” is quantō minus …, tantō minus ….

Other words

  • minor, minus — smaller, less; younger

    adjective, comparative of parvus, declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.10.42–43: sī pede major erit, subvertet, sī minor, ūret

  • pauciōrēs, pauciōra — fewer

    adjective, comparative of paucī, declension · also used · classical · Sall. Jug. 49.2: nē pauciōrēs cum plūribus manum cōnsererent (Lewis & Short)

  • plūs minus — more or less, about (with numbers)

    also used · classical · Hirt. BG 8.20; Mart. 9.100 (M-O); M-O s.v. back and forth: more or less

Examples

  • quī nōn est hodiē, crās minus aptus erit

    whoever is not ready today will be less so tomorrowOv. Rem. 94

  • adeō quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat

    so true is it that the less they had, the less they wantedLiv. praef. 12

  • Terentia minus bellē habuit, sed certum sciō jam convaluisse eam

    Terentia has been less well, but I know for certain that she is better nowDolabella in Cic. Fam. 9.9.1

  • Eō diē mīlitēs sunt paulō minus septingentī dēsīderātī.

    That day a little under seven hundred soldiers were lost.Caes. BG 7.51.4

  • magis minusve

    more or lessTraupman 347
